category_title: Adult students with high statistics anxiety and low math self-efficacy
minimal_context: The student is working in a weekly three-hour lab session to write out statistical findings and conclusions for a summary report based on a business scenario.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to write out the statistical findings and conclusions for the summary report based on the business scenario data.

STUDENT: I'm really glad we are doing this in teams. I would have probably chosen to work with a partner just to have the security of having another brain or another’s thoughts.

TUTOR: What do you think we should write for the first finding?

STUDENT: I had a hard time with that part. Usually, my partner helped me understand what the numbers actually mean.

TUTOR: Just keep trying to write it down on your own first.

STUDENT: I just can't write out the statistical verbiage and conclusions by myself. Honestly, without a collaborative partner, I would have been totally lost from day one.

options.A: Maintain a ratio of praise to correction at 3:1 or 4:1 during the weekly lab sessions.
options.B: Understand the specific origin of the student's errors to help them employ their atypical statistical strategy.
options.C: Require collaborative teams to submit joint summary reports and complete a final exam for a common grade.
options.D: Advise the student to take short breaks after every hour of the lab session, returning punctually.
